questions.stem: According to the law of conservation of mass, in a chemical reaction the total mass of the reactants is ______ the total mass of the products.
questions.explanation: Mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.

questions.stem: Which particles are found in the nucleus of an atom?
questions.explanation: The nucleus holds protons and neutrons; electrons are outside it.

questions.stem: The atomic number of an atom is the number of
questions.explanation: Atomic number (Z) is the number of protons.

questions.stem: An atom has 6 protons and 6 neutrons. What is its mass number?
questions.explanation: Mass number is the number of protons plus neutrons: 6 + 6 = 12.

questions.stem: Zn + CuSO4 -> ZnSO4 + Cu is an example of which type of reaction?
questions.explanation: Zinc displaces copper from copper sulphate.

questions.stem: Which of these metals will displace copper from copper sulphate solution?
questions.explanation: Zinc is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from its salt solution.

questions.stem: Which of these is a basic oxide?
questions.explanation: Oxides of metals are basic. CaO is a metal oxide; the others are non-metal (acidic) oxides.

questions.stem: Oxides such as ZnO and PbO react with both acids and bases. These oxides are called
Which pair of substances is used to prepare hydrogen in the laboratory?
questions.explanation: Zinc reacts with a dilute acid (not nitric acid) to give hydrogen; copper and silver do not react with these dilute acids.

questions.stem: Which substance can be used to remove the hardness of water?
Diamond and graphite are different forms of which element?
questions.explanation: Different forms of the same element are called allotropes.

questions.stem: When carbon dioxide is passed through lime water, the lime water
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide reacts with lime water to form calcium carbonate, which makes it milky.
